author: WPB1
summary: Alpha.1-era research audit (CNA 7a64362e) of project identity, language conventions, the module monorepo, the build system, renderer selection and terminology. Its current substance was already absorbed by the foundations and build deep dives and the Development repository/build pages; most counts, the renderer set, the exception bases, the Emscripten exception ABI and the vocabulary rule are stale. The residue added is a C++ dialect and error-model section re-derived at TARGET.

concepts.text: CNA describes itself as a C++ reimplementation of the XNA 4.0 programming model: a framework and runtime (not a game) that preserves the Microsoft::Xna::Framework API shape with modern C++ internals, on SDL3 by default and a pluggable renderer layer.
The name CNA is never expanded anywhere in the CNA repository; it is an opaque project name and no expansion should be invented for it.

target.evidence: README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/*.md at 009d40f5 (no expansion found)

concepts.note: The FAQ's informal 'think of it as ...' gloss has no source in the CNA repository; reported to the orchestrator.

concepts.text: FNA is the behavioural reference and genuine XNA 4.0 the tie-breaker (differential testing against FNA under tools/fna-reference); the Avatar types were ported from a decompiled XNA assembly because FNA never implemented Avatar.

Compatibility is source-shaped, not source-compatible: names, namespaces and signatures match XNA, but C# properties become getXProperty()/setXProperty() pairs and a C# game is translated, not recompiled or bridged.

README coverage figures of the alpha.1 era (227 of 245 FNA types = 92.7%, a ~90% Graphics milestone, 23 of 86 samples blocked by compiled .fx) are dated project claims that no longer describe the snapshot; the site uses the 331/331-type and 3,627/3,627-member representation census and keeps representation apart from behaviour.
concepts.note: alpha.1-era README metrics (2026-07-11); canonical numbers at 009d40f5 are the representation census in tools/audit_xna_runtime_surface.py and the pinned cna-samples plan, both already on the site.

concepts.text: C++23 is a toolchain floor rather than a feature set: CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23 is required with extensions off and propagated to consumers through cna_build_config's cxx_std_23, but no C++23-only library or language facility is used.

target.evidence: CMakeLists.txt (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD); modules/CMakeLists.txt (cna_build_config); text search of modules/ at 009d40f5

concepts.note: The alpha.1 census (zero concepts, zero requires, std::span only in spikes) is no longer true: concepts appear in Texture3D.hpp, TextureCube.hpp, GltfMaterialBridge.hpp and two content-pipeline headers, std::span has several hundred uses and std::bit_cast 58 production uses. The expansion states the TARGET census.

concepts.text: The code is written in a C++17/20 idiom: std::optional for nullable values, std::string_view, [[nodiscard]], std::span, std::bit_cast (none in the math sources, which use std::memcpy), constinit only for the Vector2 constants, std::vformat in the content pipeline.

Namespace roots: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::* and the Windows Phone root Microsoft::Devices hold the XNA surface; CNA::* holds extensions, internals and renderer/platform contracts; System::* belongs to sharp-runtime (CNA only forward-declares a few System types); SharpRuntime:: holds the mandated C#-primitive aliases.
concepts.note: Per-namespace declaration counts are alpha.1-era and not carried over.

concepts.text: Each module's include/ root reproduces the namespace path verbatim, so an #include spelling is stable public API and survived the move into modules unchanged; the renderer contract headers live under the graphics module, not a renderers/common module.
tokens: One public include root per module

concepts.text: The CNAEXT marker is defined in CNA/CNAHelper.hpp: it expands to nothing normally and to [[deprecated]] when CNA_STRICT_XNA_API is defined; anything non-XNA inside Microsoft::Xna must carry it, and XNA types never move into CNA::.
CNAHelper.hpp still carries the include guard WINDOWSPHONESPEEDYBLUPI_CNAHELPER_HPP and a May 2026 authorship stamp, a fossil of the project's Windows Phone game origin.
concepts.note: Trivia about the project's origin (include guard still present at 009d40f5); no technical consequence for readers.

concepts.text: The *EXT suffix is a naming convention independent of the CNAEXT macro in both directions: marked members without the suffix exist (ShaderEffect and others) and suffixed members without the mark exist; the macro, not the suffix, is the reliable signal. Alpha.1 grep counts of CNAEXT lines are not carried over.
tokens: The EXT suffix is a naming convention

target.evidence: CNAEXT.md; modules/*/include at 009d40f5 (checked by the catalogue page)

concepts.text: Porting obligations of the marker: C++ iterator support (begin/end/size_type), GetTypeName() on System::Object subclasses and C# internal constants re-exposed as public static constexpr (for example GamePad::LeftDeadZone, TouchPanel::MAX_TOUCHES) are CNAEXT because C++ has no assembly visibility.

'CNAEXT' names more than one thing: the always-compiled marker convention in Microsoft::Xna, and the opt-in CNA_CNAEXT engine layer (CNA::Graphics in modules/graphics-ext); per-draw shading that fits an XNA Effect ships always, frame-level orchestration sits behind the option.
concepts.note: The catalogue now distinguishes three mechanisms and the engine layer grew from 12 to 98 public headers; the two-meaning table of alpha.1 is superseded.

concepts.text: The strict-API check is not a user-facing CMake option: CNA_STRICT_XNA_API is a compile definition on two harness targets in cmake/Harnesses.cmake, one that must compile and one (StrictXnaApiSurfaceLeakCheck_MustFailToCompile, WILL_FAIL) that must fail, run only with GNU/Clang and reaching only the members its checked files use.

Exception hierarchy: sharp-runtime's System::Exception derives from std::exception (not std::runtime_error) and ports System.Exception's fields (HResult 0x80131500, inner exception as std::exception_ptr) without GetBaseException/ToString; CNAException derives from it.

The XNA-native exception types split across two roots: at alpha.1 the graphics device exceptions derived from std::runtime_error, at this snapshot they derive from System::Exception, while ContentLoadException still derives from std::runtime_error.
concepts.note: Corrected: DeviceLostException/NoSuitableGraphicsDeviceException now derive from System::Exception; the site lists both families at TARGET.

concepts.text: The two exception families split by layer: most std::runtime_error throws are in modules/renderers ('this renderer cannot do that'), while the public wrappers throw the .NET-shaped System types an XNA program expects.

target.evidence: throw-site search of non-test, non-example sources under modules/ at 009d40f5 (1,393 of 1,746 std::runtime_error throws in renderers)

concepts.note: Alpha.1 counts replaced by TARGET counts; renderers now also throw System::NotSupportedException at many sites, which the expansion says.

concepts.text: Use after disposal has two conventions: System::ObjectDisposedException in graphics, graphics-ext, audio, gamer-services, net, devices, media and content (one renderer site), but std::runtime_error in the runtime module's Game, as the repository's CLAUDE.md coding rule still prescribes.

target.evidence: CLAUDE.md (disposal rule); modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp (AssertNotDisposed); throw-site search at 009d40f5

concepts.text: IGraphicsRenderer's default virtual bodies throw (SetData32, ReadBackbuffer, instancing and other optional operations), making 'refuse loudly instead of approximating' load-bearing renderer policy; public wrappers may translate a refusal into System::NotSupportedException.

There is no project-wide noexcept policy (the keyword sits mostly on move operations); VideoPlayer::Dispose() is kept idempotent rather than copying FNA's throw on a second call, because the destructor disposes again and destructors are implicitly noexcept.

Emscripten exception model: the alpha.1 build compiled with native WebAssembly exceptions (-fwasm-exceptions) to match the easy-gl chain; at this snapshot CNA uses the JavaScript-lowered model (-fexceptions, DISABLE_EXCEPTION_CATCHING=0) through a scoped interface target.
concepts.note: Corrected: -fwasm-exceptions is no longer the model; the site states the TARGET ABI.

concepts.text: Ownership follows the XNA API: buffers and SpriteBatch own their renderer object uniquely, while Texture2D/TextureCube hold a shared_ptr and keep defaulted copy operations because game code copies textures by value; the device-to-renderer seam is a unique_ptr from CreateGraphicsRenderer.

GraphicsResource mirrors XNA's IDisposable pattern on sharp-runtime's base: GPU handles are released by Dispose(), the destructor runs Dispose(false) without raising the disposal events, and GraphicsDevice keeps a non-owning list of raw resource pointers that it disposes on teardown.

C# events map to sharp-runtime's System::EventHandler<TEventArgs> (subscribe with operator+=, fire with Raise/Invoke); C# internal maps to private/protected/detail namespaces, never public C++; C# interfaces become abstract base classes.
The repository is a module monorepo; configure fails if the legacy global src/ or include/ trees reappear, and consumer include spelling did not change in the move.

Module and renderer counts of alpha.1 (14 framework modules; 42 renderer families carrying 46 identities) are superseded: the declared lists at this snapshot hold 22 framework modules and 21 renderer families (plus common/d3d and common/mojoshader) carrying 25 public identities.
concepts.note: Corrected counts; the proximity of identity and family counts that confused alpha.1 prose is handled on the site by always naming both.

concepts.text: cna_add_module() creates a static library with a CNA::<Alias> alias and exactly one PUBLIC include root (the module's own include/); no module's src/ is ever an include root, so cross-module internal headers live under include/CNA/Internal.
gamer-services and net hand-roll CNA_GamerServices / CNA_Net targets instead of the cna_<name> naming produced by cna_add_module.

The shared build-flags interface is definitions-only (no include directories); at alpha.1 it was cna_build_flags with unconditional SOUND_ENABLED and XNA5, at this snapshot it is cna_build_config / CNA::BuildConfig carrying cxx_std_23, XNA5 and the renderer and feature defines.
concepts.note: Corrected name and content; SOUND_ENABLED is no longer unconditional (SDL3 and ALSA audio only).

concepts.text: Umbrella targets: CNA (the full-framework INTERFACE umbrella that keeps target_link_libraries(game CNA) working), CNA::CnaExt (formerly the NoXna composition) and the build-flags interface.

Three deliberate static-archive cycles are declared on both sides so CMake repeats archives on the link line: graphics-core with input (GraphicsDevice updates TouchPanel/Mouse binding, MouseCursor uses Texture2D), audio with media (FrameworkDispatcher pumps MediaPlayer), and graphics-core with the selected renderer (factory edge plus header-inlined defaults).

Renderer composition machinery: at alpha.1 one selected family directory was entered and globbed non-recursively into RENDERER_TARGET; at this snapshot cna_configure_renderer_identity() runs per identity so a multi-renderer build can link a compatible set.
concepts.note: Corrected: per-identity macro and CNA_RENDERER_TARGETS lists replace the single-family entry.

concepts.text: The one documented physical-ownership exception: GDI compiles the software family's 2D translation units published as CNA_GDI_SOFTWARE_SOURCES while ownership stays with modules/renderers/software; DIRECTX11 and DIRECTX12 share cna_renderer_d3dcommon.
Location is ownership: a configure-time source-partition validator globs every .cpp/.mm under modules/ and fails unless it sits in a declared module's or renderer family's src/, tests/ or examples/.

Module probes each register a link-and-run test and a link-closure test with forbid regexes; the sharpest contracts are storage (no other libcna_ archive on its line) and devices-ext (an escaped dot so it never depends on the XNA devices base); extra gates require ENet for net and both halves of CnaExt.
concepts.note: Probe count is fifteen at TARGET (fourteen at alpha.1).

concepts.text: The link-closure gate reads <build>/CMakeFiles/<target>.dir/link.txt and exits 77 (CTest skip) when it is absent, so under the Ninja generator used by presets and CI every ModuleLinkClosure test skips instead of running.
Include reachability and header self-containment are checked by tools under modularization/tools, not by standing gates.

Alpha.1 test-layout counts (419 module-owned test TUs, only 14 of 42 renderer families with tests, a 157-file top-level tests/ tree) are superseded; the CnaTests corpus has no configuration-free size and the site reports canonical static counts.
concepts.note: Canonical: 904 test source files, 12,610 static GoogleTest-family definitions (site method).

concepts.text: The 2026-08-10 physical-modularization campaign: seven pure-rename commits (1,776 files), a pivotal build rewrite that deleted the global library CMake files, a probe fleet grown from 5 to 14, and a reconciliation recording 1,357 to 1,357 production TUs with zero ctest removals.
concepts.note: Campaign chronology of 2026-08-10, before alpha.1; the site's module-architecture history section summarises the outcome and the paths that no longer exist.

concepts.text: Two later campaigns are often conflated with the modularization: module-owned example registration (deleting cmake/Examples.cmake and dozens of per-renderer test manifests) and the backend-to-renderer terminology rename.
concepts.note: Campaign history (2026-08-10); current example ownership and names are documented on the site.

concepts.text: Examples live with the module whose API they demonstrate (graphics owns the renderer-agnostic conformance fixtures and shared support headers); top-level examples/ keeps only the examples/golden oracle corpus, loaded through working-directory-relative paths.

Per-module ownership table: core (CNAEXT marker, Logger, platform/renderer identity enums, PathContainment), math, graphics (XNA Graphics plus the renderer contract headers), input, audio (which owns FrameworkDispatcher to avoid a runtime-audio cycle), media, content, storage (headers-only on core), runtime (Game and the loop, top of the stack), devices, devices-ext, graphics-ext, gamer-services, net.
concepts.note: The TARGET table also has platform, content-pipeline, design, diagnostics, inspector, phone, video-ffmpeg and c-api.

concepts.text: Each module links a narrow set of sharp-runtime components (for example math only Core.Base, gamer-services Core.Base, IO, Collections.Core, Globalization, Runtime, Threading) through cna_link_sharp_runtime instead of the whole library.
devices-ext deliberately never links the XNA devices base and the reverse never happens; storage links core headers only (PlayerIndex, CNAEXT, PathContainment) so its closure stays exact.
tokens: Two negative contracts worth reading closely

concepts.text: Requirements: CMake 3.20 or newer and a C++23 compiler with extensions off; alpha.1 prose named GCC 12+/Clang 15+, and the always-built content code needs a current standard library for <format>.
The C++ framework has no install(), export() or CPack rules; a game consumes it with add_subdirectory plus target_link_libraries(game CNA); only the C API module installs a package.

target.evidence: CMakeLists.txt, cmake/, modules/*/CMakeLists.txt; modules/c-api/CMakeLists.txt (install, CNAConfig) at 009d40f5

concepts.note: Corrected: the C API module now has install/export rules; the C++ framework still has none.

concepts.text: Compilers exercised by CI at alpha.1 (GCC 14, Clang, AppleClang, MSVC, MinGW-w64 GCC, emcc) and the GNU/Clang-only strict-API harness.
concepts.note: The CI inventory changed (20 workflows, 28 jobs at TARGET); the site's CI page is authoritative.

concepts.section: 3.2 Every CNA option with default and effect
concepts.text: Root options with defaults: CNA_USE_CCACHE ON (sets the compiler launchers only if unset, before sharp-runtime is added), CNA_BUILD_TESTS ON, CNA_BUILD_EXAMPLES ON, CNA_CNAEXT OFF, CNA_DEVICES OFF, CNA_ENABLE_NET ON, CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_ROOT defaulting to ../sharp-runtime.

concepts.section: 3.2 Every CNA option with default and effect
concepts.text: Without CNA_DEVICES the whole CNA::Devices extension surface (file dialogs, message boxes, clipboard, tray) compiles out without a diagnostic, which is why the sanitizer presets set it explicitly.

concepts.section: 3.2 Every CNA option with default and effect
concepts.text: CNA_TEST_DISPLAY bakes a DISPLAY value (default :0, with SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11) into every window-creating test's environment; set :99 for Xvfb.

concepts.section: 3.2 Every CNA option with default and effect
concepts.text: CNA_SANITIZE takes a comma list (for example address,undefined) and is applied after the vendored SDL and ENet are configured, so those stay uninstrumented.

concepts.section: 3.2 Every CNA option with default and effect
concepts.text: SDL options: CNA_USE_SYSTEM_SDL switches to find_package, CNA_MAX_VENDORED_BUILD_JOBS caps the configure-time vendored build (validated as a positive integer), and CNA_SDL_PREBUILT_ROOT keys the persistent SDL install root by target system and processor so a cross build cannot overwrite the native cache.

concepts.section: 3.2 Every CNA option with default and effect
concepts.text: Selection options: CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER with a platform default, one CNA_RENDERER_<NAME> boolean per identity, plus sub-selectors of retired renderer families (a GL-API chooser and a raster/GPU mode switch) and a retired family's shader-compiler toggle.
concepts.note: The sub-selector options belonged to renderer families retired before 009d40f5 (cmake/RendererIdentities.cmake lists them as retired); the current selection options are on the CMake options reference.

concepts.section: 3.2 Every CNA option with default and effect
concepts.text: Third-party pin options for current renderers: CNA_FNA3D_GIT_TAG / repository for FNA3D and CNA_WEBGPU_VERSION / CNA_WEBGPU_ROOT / CNA_WEBGPU_AUTO_DOWNLOAD (ON: downloads wgpu-native at configure time; a root makes the build offline and reproducible).

concepts.section: 3.2 Every CNA option with default and effect
concepts.text: Most alpha.1 third-party pin, root and patch options (Git tags and roots for about ten native libraries, three engine patch toggles, an auto-fetch switch) served renderer families that are retired at this snapshot.
concepts.note: Options of retired renderer families; refused or absent at 009d40f5 (cmake/RendererIdentities.cmake retired list).

concepts.section: 3.2 Every CNA option with default and effect
concepts.text: Module-local options: CNA_BUILD_HTML_DOM_HOST_TESTS and CNA_BUILD_SVG_DOM_HOST_TESTS (OFF) add host-side tests of the DOM renderers; CNA_DIRECT2D_TEST_RUNTIME chooses WINE or PROTON for the cross-compiled Direct2D tests.

concepts.section: 3.2 Every CNA option with default and effect
concepts.text: Internal cache variables (RENDERER_DIR, RENDERER_TARGET, CNA_RENDERER_DEFINE, CNA_FFMPEG_AVAILABLE, CNA_DRACO_AVAILABLE, CNA_GRAPHICS_EXAMPLES_DIR and others) are implementation state, not user-facing options.

Outside code enters a build through five mechanisms: git submodules (SDL, SDL_image, SDL_mixer, googletest; Draco at this snapshot), vendored in-tree sources (cgltf, stb, ENet, wgpu-native), sibling checkouts, FetchContent or configure-time downloads, and host packages.
tokens: Five ways outside code enters a build
concepts.note: Draco became a submodule after alpha.1.

concepts.text: Missing-submodule guards stop configure with an actionable message, and note that a ZIP or tarball export cannot contain submodule content at all.

FFmpeg availability is a computed gate that changes which files compile: at alpha.1 it was forced off on MinGW/Win32/Emscripten/Android (to keep the host's FFmpeg out of cross builds) and dropped the video TUs; at this snapshot CNA_ENABLE_VIDEO and the video-ffmpeg module govern it and Video types throw NotSupportedException without a backend.
tokens: Host packages can change what compiles
concepts.note: Corrected mechanism; the canonical FFmpeg row is on the site.

concepts.text: Draco is optional: without it a Draco-compressed glTF primitive is refused with a clear unsupported-format error at import time.

SDL3, SDL3_image and SDL3_mixer are configured, built and installed during cmake configure into a persistent prefix outside every build tree (so a clean build keeps it), with every optional codec disabled, which is also why a recursive submodule update is unnecessary.
tokens: The configure-time SDL build and what it implies

concepts.text: At alpha.1 about ten native libraries were fetched or located per renderer family (with patches applied at configure time); the current renderer dependencies are FNA3D (fetched), wgpu-native (downloaded or rooted), Vulkan and GL SDKs, and the sibling libraries.
concepts.note: Most alpha.1 fetch rows belonged to retired renderer families.

concepts.text: sharp-runtime is always required, located by CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_ROOT (default ../sharp-runtime), is not a submodule, and a missing checkout stops configure with the clone command.

easy-gl (with its own meta-gl sibling) is needed only for the five GL identities and free-direct (with free-api underneath) only for FREEDIRECT; both are found at fixed sibling paths and a missing one stops configure with the clone line.

sharp-runtime consumption seam: cna_link_sharp_runtime(<target> <scope> [components]) links component targets of the modular sharp-runtime, with a CNA-wide default closure when none are named; the older monolithic shape was a single SHARP_RUNTIME archive.

cmake/toolchains/mingw-w64.cmake targets 64-bit Windows (preferring x86_64-w64-mingw32 tools, falling back to i686) with find-root modes ONLY for libraries and headers; no Android or Emscripten toolchain file is vendored (emcmake or the SDK files are used).
The 32-bit MinGW toolchain file existed at alpha.1 as the required ABI of a retired renderer family that carried its window handle in a 32-bit integer.
concepts.note: The ABI requirement belonged to a retired renderer family; the current toolchain files and their uses are on the site's configuring page.

concepts.text: The presets file itself warns that the CnaTests binary, not ctest, is the authoritative runner: ctest runs each discovered case in its own process and reports unbuilt display-dependent executables as failures.
The alpha.1 sanitizer presets passed raw -fsanitize flags instead of CNA_SANITIZE and required CNA_DEVICES=ON because their surface otherwise compiled out.

concepts.text: Submodules are initialised non-recursively (git submodule update --init): the project disables every optional codec in its SDL_image/SDL_mixer arguments, and --recursive only adds about 19 nested codec submodules and measured 6-7x slower.
Verified command lines for the Linux default, SDL_RENDERER, system SDL, MinGW cross build, the web preset, the Ninja test preset, sanitizers and the extension layers.

concepts.text: Public renderer identities are held in several registries that must agree (the CMake identity list, GraphicsRendererType.hpp, the C ABI header) and scripts/check_renderer_identities.py holds them to one canonical table, registered as the RendererIdentityRegistry test.
concepts.note: Corrected: 25 identities; the C ABI header joined the registries and retired values stay reserved.

concepts.text: A gap in the old DirectX identity numbering was deliberate, and the historical enum order was accreted rather than alphabetical.
concepts.note: Concerned identities retired before 009d40f5; the TARGET enum order follows C ABI values.

concepts.text: Two selection surfaces: -DCNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER=<IDENTITY> or one CNA_RENDERER_<NAME>=ON boolean; if any boolean is ON exactly one must be, it overrides CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER, and an unknown value stops configure.
Default renderer by platform: WEBGL2 under Emscripten, OPENGLES3 on Linux, SDL_RENDERER everywhere else (Windows and macOS included).

Each identity sets RENDERER_DIR (a path string), RENDERER_TARGET (the static library), a CNA_RENDERER_<X> compile definition and CNA_RENDERER_DEFINE, which the build-config interface re-exports to every module and consumer.

The five GL identities share the EasyGL family and CNA_RENDERER_EASYGL; a CNA_GL_PROFILE_<IDENTITY> definition keeps them distinguishable and a constexpr getCurrentGraphicsRendererType() decodes the pair back into the public enum; EASYGL itself is not a selector.

Current platform gates: Direct3D, Direct2D and GDI identities need a Windows target, METAL needs macOS, the browser identities need Emscripten, and the desktop GL identities are refused under Emscripten in favour of WEBGL1/WEBGL2.

Platform gates, warnings and a 32-bit requirement that applied to retired renderer families, and sub-selectors that chose a native API or raster/GPU mode inside a retired family (including a self-inconsistent value list).
concepts.note: All concern renderer families retired before 009d40f5 (cmake/RendererIdentities.cmake).

concepts.text: check_renderer_identities.py compares the C++ enum order-sensitively but the CMake list as a set (its order is cosmetic), so any addition, removal or rename fails until the canonical table and the documented count are updated deliberately.

The 2026-08-10 rename chain: graphics backend to renderer (types, paths, namespaces, CMake names), DirectX identity normalisation, OPENGLES to OPENGLES3, NOXNA to CNAEXT, then fix-ups restoring historical prose.
concepts.note: Rename chronology before alpha.1; the old-to-new names that still matter (D3D9 to DIRECTX9, CNA_GRAPHICS_BACKEND to CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER, EASYGL to five GL profiles) are on the site.

concepts.text: Old spellings have no compatibility aliases: an old selector such as D3D9 or EASYGL stops configure, and old type names do not compile.

concepts.text: A one-paragraph vocabulary for readers: renderer identities implemented by families under modules/renderers, selected by CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER, reached through IGraphicsRenderer; a renderer's own internal drivers are not CNA identities.

concepts.text: docs/graphics-resource-lifetime.md in the CNA repository describes exclusive unique_ptr ownership for every resource, but the texture classes share their renderer object through shared_ptr; reset() on a shared handle drops rather than destroys.
concepts.note: Doc drift in the CNA repository already recorded by WP08; the site states the real model.

concepts.text: CLAUDE.md's disposal rule (throw std::runtime_error after disposal) disagrees with the XNA-faithful System::ObjectDisposedException most modules throw; the runtime module follows the rule.
XNA-native exception base classes split across System::Exception and std::runtime_error without being listed as a deliberate deviation.
concepts.note: Graphics device exceptions moved to System::Exception; ContentLoadException remains std::runtime_error, as the site states.
